investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Limit (409 Conflict) — All Remote-Agents Checks Failing
investigation.summary: Every POST /api/agents call made by the remote-agents eval suite is being rejected with HTTP 409 and the error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100", meaning the eval org has reached the swarm's per-org agent quota ceiling and no new remote agents can be created. Because all three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) share the same agent-creation step as their entry point and all carry the identical 409 error message, the failure is a shared upstream dependency failure at the POST /api/agents endpoint, not an isolated eval infrastructure issue.
investigation.rootCause: The production-api swarm backend is returning HTTP 409 with code "conflict" and message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" for every POST /api/agents request issued by the eval runner. The eval org used by the status probes has accumulated 100 swarm agents and the backend is enforcing a hard limit of 100, preventing any new agent from being created. Because remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime all depend on successfully creating a new remote agent as their first step (evidenced by the createAgent call at run-status-probes.mjs:1339), none of them can proceed past the creation call, and all produce zero evidence — leaving orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, and remoteState entirely absent from the eval output.

sibling.remote-agent-state and sibling.remote-agent-runtime carry the exact same 409 message (sameMessage: true), establishing that all three checks share the same failure point at POST /api/agents.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=1244 — the call returned in ~1.2 s, consistent with a fast synchronous quota rejection rather than a timeout or VM provisioning failure.
possibleCauses: Most likely: The eval org's swarm agent count has reached the hard limit of 100. Prior eval runs created agents that were not cleaned up (e.g., due to withCleanup failures, interrupted runs, or cleanup bugs), causing agents to accumulate until the quota was exhausted.

Less likely but possible: The eval runner's withCleanup mechanism is functioning but the quota was reached by legitimate agent accumulation across many scheduled runs without sufficient cleanup between them.

Least likely given the evidence: A backend quota configuration change lowered the per-org limit to a value already exceeded by the eval org's existing agents, causing previously passing runs to start failing — however, no history of a prior passing run exists (lastPassingAt: null, previousRunCount: 0), so this cannot be confirmed or ruled out from the available data.

investigation.summary: The image-generation-stream eval for the production-api runtime environment failed because the agent runtime harness returned a 404 on session open, causing the stream to emit a generation_error frame with code SESSION_OPEN_FAILED instead of the required generation_completed frame and an artifact URL. Both contract assertions — frameTypes containing "generation_completed" and imageUrlPresent equaling true — were violated as a direct consequence of this upstream session-open failure.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Limit (409 Conflict) — All Remote-Agents Checks Failing
investigations.summary: Every POST /api/agents call made by the remote-agents eval suite is being rejected with HTTP 409 and the error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100", meaning the eval org has reached the swarm's per-org agent quota ceiling and no new remote agents can be created. Because all three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) share the same agent-creation step as their entry point and all carry the identical 409 error message, the failure is a shared upstream dependency failure at the POST /api/agents endpoint, not an isolated eval infrastructure issue.
investigations.rootCause: The production-api swarm backend is returning HTTP 409 with code "conflict" and message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" for every POST /api/agents request issued by the eval runner. The eval org used by the status probes has accumulated 100 swarm agents and the backend is enforcing a hard limit of 100, preventing any new agent from being created. Because remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime all depend on successfully creating a new remote agent as their first step (evidenced by the createAgent call at run-status-probes.mjs:1339), none of them can proceed past the creation call, and all produce zero evidence — leaving orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, and remoteState entirely absent from the eval output.

possibleCauses: Most likely: The eval org's swarm agent count has reached the hard limit of 100. Prior eval runs created agents that were not cleaned up (e.g., due to withCleanup failures, interrupted runs, or cleanup bugs), causing agents to accumulate until the quota was exhausted.

Less likely but possible: The eval runner's withCleanup mechanism is functioning but the quota was reached by legitimate agent accumulation across many scheduled runs without sufficient cleanup between them.

Least likely given the evidence: A backend quota configuration change lowered the per-org limit to a value already exceeded by the eval org's existing agents, causing previously passing runs to start failing — however, no history of a prior passing run exists (lastPassingAt: null, previousRunCount: 0), so this cannot be confirmed or ruled out from the available data.

investigations.title: Image Generation Stream Eval Failure: SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) on /api/generate/image/stream in production-api
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval for the production-api runtime environment failed because the agent runtime harness returned a 404 on session open, causing the stream to emit a generation_error frame with code SESSION_OPEN_FAILED instead of the required generation_completed frame and an artifact URL. Both contract assertions — frameTypes containing "generation_completed" and imageUrlPresent equaling true — were violated as a direct consequence of this upstream session-open failure.
investigations.rootCause: The agent runtime endpoint backing /api/generate/image/stream is unreachable or returning HTTP 404 in the production-api environment at the time of the eval run. The stream correctly initiated (generation_start was emitted) but immediately failed to open a session (SESSION_OPEN_FAILED), preventing any image generation from proceeding and making it impossible for the stream to emit generation_completed or an artifact URL. This is an eval-observed infrastructure or configuration failure localized to the agent runtime harness reachability in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so a broader production outage cannot be asserted.
proof: failed-check.evidence: generation_error frame carries code SESSION_OPEN_FAILED and message 'agent runtime endpoint not found (404): the harness is unreachable or running an incompatible version. Verify the harness deployment and the LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL configuration.'

failed-check.evidence: imageUrlPresent = false, violating the contract assertion at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 272.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=2249, far below the warningLatencyMs=180000 threshold, confirming the failure is an immediate hard error at session-open time, not a timeout.
failed-check.message: contract validation error explicitly states both assertion failures: frameTypes expected to contain 'generation_completed'; imageUrlPresent expected true but got false.

possibleCauses: The agent runtime harness is not deployed or is misconfigured in the production-api environment, causing the /api/generate/image/stream endpoint to return 404 when attempting to open a session (strongest evidence: SESSION_OPEN_FAILED with explicit 404 message in failed-check.evidence).

The SWARM_BASE_URL or LOCAL_HARNESS_URL environment variable used by the eval runner is missing, empty, or pointing to a stale/incorrect host for the production-api environment, causing the 404 at session-open time (supported by the error message text in failed-check.evidence).

The agent runtime harness is deployed but running an incompatible version that no longer exposes the session-open endpoint at the expected path, causing a 404 (supported by the error message text in failed-check.evidence).

The image generation route /api/generate/image/stream requires an agent runtime session that is provisioned on-demand, and the provisioning step itself is failing with a 404 before any generation work begins (consistent with SESSION_OPEN_FAILED occurring immediately after generation_start, as shown in failed-check.evidence).
